  are fair. Gate fidelity, atom loss/loading, laser control, cryogenic electronics, material disorder, exchange
  variability, and readout/connectivity deserve enough specificity to make “demanding” informative.
- **Topological qubits:** “Elegant protection if realized, experimentally uncertain” is commendably calibrated. Separate
  topological hardware/non-Abelian anyons from topological QEC such as surface codes, which is already experimentally
  implemented without intrinsically topological qubits.
- **Leaderboard refusal:** This is the right editorial decision. Even qualitative “bargains” age and depend on benchmark
  definitions; timestamp and source them, or replace competitive judgments with invariant engineering dimensions.
- **Qubit count:** Correctly rejects raw count and names error/connectivity/fidelity/coherence/calibration/QEC context.
  Add logical error per operation, executable circuit volume/depth, parallelism, uptime/yield, reset, leakage, decoding,
  application success, and total runtime. Gate “fidelity” and “error rates” partly duplicate each other and require
  comparable characterization protocols.
- **Reader entertainment: 4/5.** The rapid tour and “different bargain” framing are highly skimmable. Platform lists are
  inherently catalog-like; the systems-stack sentence gives them a stronger narrative purpose.
- **Unit completion:** Lines 1163–1207 inspected through the split DiVincenzo sentence, including every platform claim,
  all six bargain bullets, anti-leaderboard rationale, and qubit-count metric.

##### §0.15 — criteria, NISQ, Sycamore, and present-tense posture (lines 1208–1264)

- **DiVincenzo criteria:** The five computational criteria are correctly summarized, and the two communication criteria
  are gestured at rather than listed. Since the sentence explicitly says “checklist,” enumerate ability to interconvert
  stationary/flying qubits and faithfully transmit flying qubits, or say this chapter uses only the computation subset.
  Verify whether “codified in his 2000 implementation review” matches preprint/publication dates.
- **Coherence ratio:** “Long coherence relative to gate times” is the intended criterion, but QEC cares about full error
  channels and operation fidelity, not one \(T_2/t_g\) ratio. Measurement, preparation/reset, leakage, crosstalk and
  classical feedback show why the criteria are framing rather than a product spec.
- **Snapshot note:** Explicit June 2026 dating and refusal of a live leaderboard are excellent maintenance practice. A
  stale snapshot embedded in an archived draft should still say “archived; verify against...” and link durable benchmark
  methodology, not leave “current device documentation” to vendor-selected evidence alone.
- **Cloud access/NISQ:** Cloud processors did broaden hands-on access in the 2010s/2020s. Preskill’s primary paper was
  published in 2018 and defined 50–100-qubit noisy devices whose reliable circuit size is limited; cite
  [Preskill 2018](https://doi.org/10.22331/Q-2018-08-06-79). “Popularised” is plausible but should distinguish coining the
  term from dissemination.
- **NISQ definition drift:** “Enough qubits to be scientifically interesting” is subjective, and today some devices
  contain early logical-QEC experiments while remaining far from large fault-tolerant workloads. Frame NISQ as a dated
  era/concept rather than a crisp machine class defined solely by qubit count.
- **Sycamore facts:** The primary paper reports 53 active superconducting qubits, roughly 200 seconds for one million
  samples, and an initial classical estimate of ~10,000 years—not merely unspecified “minutes” and “far longer.” Cite
  [Arute et al. 2019](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-019-1666-5) and preserve “authors estimated,” as the draft
  does, because later classical algorithms/hardware altered comparisons.
- **Task/claim precision:** Random-circuit sampling was a narrow sampling/verification benchmark; “reproduce” needs the
  same fidelity/sample criterion. “Not a useful business application” is reasonable but “useful” is value-laden; it was
  scientifically/benchmark useful. “Quantum advantage” is not simply a polite synonym—definitions vary over provable,
  empirical, useful, and end-to-end advantage.
- **Milestone judgment:** Saying comparison became empirical/contested is fair. One experiment did not establish quantum
  advantage broadly or rule out future simulation; the text appropriately contains the claim, but “real moment” remains
  editorial and should be explicitly the authors’/field’s assessment.
- **Present-state claim:** “Today’s machines mostly offer noisy physical qubits...” is a June 2026 snapshot requiring
  evidence across platforms. Below-threshold logical-memory demonstrations do not yet equal general fault-tolerant
  computers, but the binary physical-versus-logical wording now misses early logical-qubit experiments. Say useful-scale,
  universal logical computation remains unavailable publicly and define evidence.
- **Engineering stack:** Circuit→compiler→pulse→calibration→runtime→mitigation/QEC decoder→classical co-processing is an
  excellent end-to-end list. Add characterization/verification, scheduling, resource estimation, fabrication/packaging,
  data movement, security, operations, and reproducibility; “applications” are consumers rather than stack layer.
- **Hype posture:** Neither hype nor cynicism is the right stance, and the callout’s parallel “real” clauses read well.
  “Algorithms are real” should distinguish mathematical algorithms from demonstrated useful implementations; “path to
  scalability” is conditional on threshold assumptions and acceptable overhead.
- **Bullet recap:** “Quantum information is operational” is vague; name teleportation/QKD/QEC primitives. “Hardware
  progress is substantial” needs dated metrics rather than assertion. “Useful, general, fault-tolerant” bundles three
  separate targets and invites disagreement over “useful”; define each or say large-scale fault-tolerant general-purpose.
- **Closing gap:** Beautiful abstraction versus noisy system is memorable and honest. The chapter repeatedly uses this
  same gap/reversal structure; variation here could keep the rhetorical pattern from becoming predictable.
- **Reader entertainment: 4.5/5.** Sycamore supplies a concrete contested milestone and the calibrated-excitement box is
  memorable. The concluding affirmations verge on manifesto, but the frank gap keeps them credible.
- **Section completion:** Lines 1208–1264 inspected in full, including the carried DiVincenzo criteria, dated snapshot,
  cloud/NISQ history, every Sycamore claim (externally checked), engineering-stack component, callout, six bullets, and
  final sentence.

##### §0.16 — What This History Gives the Practicing Developer

- **Purpose:** The return to the developer and “map of why” fulfill the opening contract. This is synthesis rather than
  new content, but it should point to exact forthcoming chapters so the history becomes navigation rather than a second
  generic summary.
- **“Forced” history:** Failed models motivated new theory, but underdetermination, rival formalisms, interpretation, and
  creative mathematical choices mean quantum mechanics was not logically forced in one inevitable form. Replace
  “forced/replaced” with “developed to account for” and “generalized/superseded in microscopic regimes.”
- **Trajectory/property binary:** Quantum theory still supports semiclassical trajectories, wave-packet centers,
  eigenstate properties, and trajectory formulations; standard formalism does not generally assign simultaneous sharp
  values to incompatible observables. The qualified formulation belongs here, especially after the review repeatedly
  found the draft’s categorical version.
- **Entanglement/resource recap:** Correct at narrative scale but resource value is protocol/operation-dependent. The
  technology list again mixes quantum-enabled classical devices with coherent quantum-information systems; that is the
  intended point, but “modern materials” is too broad to carry explanatory content.
- **Great-person compression:** Turing/Shannon/Landauer/Bennett create a memorable lineage while obscuring Church,
  reversible-logic contributors, coding theorists, experimentalists, and parallel traditions. “Almost inevitable” is
  Whiggish: the question looks inevitable only retrospectively. Say the convergence made the question natural and
  tractable.
- **Anti-magic paragraph:** Short sentences provide excellent cadence. “Uses entanglement” is not universal, “measures
  carefully” is vague, and “fights noise” anthropomorphizes engineering; “may exploit entanglement, designs measurement,
  and manages/corrects noise” is accurate without losing energy.
- **Engineering-order prescription:** Model→operations→circuits→algorithms→noise→hardware is clear, but error correction,
  complexity, applications, classical integration, and validation deserve placement. “Should” conflicts with the actual
  book if its order differs; describe this book’s verified sequence rather than legislate an abstract text.
- **State bullet:** “Not a classical record...” is broadly helpful but interpretive/categorical; insert “in the standard
  operational formalism, not generally.” Classical records can also encode distributions rather than definite
  properties.
- **Amplitude bullet:** Amplitudes combine for indistinguishable alternatives and the Born rule yields probabilities;
  they do not universally “interfere before probabilities appear.” The phase emphasis is good and should mention basis/
  experimental context.
- **Measurement/noise bullet:** Both are represented by physical processes/channels, but measurement is not the same kind
  of operation as uncontrolled noise and annotations can describe rather than cause either. “Not passive annotations” is
  rhetoric; “must be included in the operational model” is exact.
- **Entanglement bullet:** Nonseparability and no-signalling are correctly paired. Classical correlations are also joint
  structure, so say “nonseparable quantum structure” and remind that classical comparison is needed to observe Bell-type
  correlations.
- **Physical-information bullet:** Good Landauer payoff if abstract information versus physical instantiation remains
  distinct. Physical limits include thermodynamics, causality, noise, precision and control; not all follow from the
  slogan alone.
- **Reliable-stack bullet:** This is perhaps the best practical takeaway: advantage requires algorithmic structure plus
  an end-to-end stack. Add efficient input/output and a better classical baseline, which often decide usefulness.
- **Later-chapter reminders:** Vector/tensor formalism did not merely “survive failure”; it was constructed and justified
  by empirical success. Unitary reversibility is only ideal closed evolution. Reading-as-interaction is a good warning
  but nondemolition/commuting measurements exist. Syndrome learning rather than logical reading accurately captures QEC.
- **Final correspondence statement:** “Successful approximation pushed past its domain” is excellent and corrects much
  earlier binary rhetoric. “Replacement theory” should become “more general theory,” and “substrate” should acknowledge
  classical support/control. “Engineering surface” is memorable but undefined; it works as a final metaphor if not
  treated as a technical claim.
- **Reader entertainment: 4.5/5.** The terse anti-magic cadence and recurring-reversal payoff make a strong ending. It
  repeats several earlier maps nearly verbatim, so a shorter synthesis plus forward links could produce a sharper finish.
- **Section completion:** Lines 1265–1322 inspected in full, including both historical recaps, anti-magic paragraph,
  engineering sequence, all six takeaway bullets, every forward reminder, correspondence argument, and final metaphor.

##### References — scope and entries through measurement-based computation (lines 1323–1370)

- **Declared role:** Saying the list “anchored” claims is stronger than the manuscript demonstrates because assertions
  have no inline citation markers. A bibliography proves possible consultation, not which source supports which sentence;
  add footnotes/endnote keys and access/verification dates.
- **Source hierarchy:** Nobel/APS/Computer History Museum summaries are accessible tertiary/institutional accounts, not
  substitutes for Planck, Einstein, Rutherford/Geiger–Marsden, Compton, or transistor primary papers and modern
  historiography. Use them for orientation, then cite editions/translations and peer-reviewed histories for disputed
  motivations/priority.
- **Planck entry:** The Nobel biography can support broad biography but not the draft’s detailed claim about quantized
  oscillator energy or Planck’s “mood.” Cite the 1900 papers/translation and historical scholarship; the current link’s
  “especially...” annotation is not a bibliographic locator.
- **Einstein entry:** A Nobel facts page supports the prize motivation, not a rigorous account of the 1905 light-quantum
  hypothesis/photoelectric equation or the later word “photon.” Add the paper and Millikan-era experimental evidence.
- **Rutherford entry:** APS News is secondary popular history and its 2006 date should be included. The URL/title alone
  cannot substantiate all nuclear-atom/atomic-collapse claims; cite the 1911 paper and clarify scattering contributors.
- **Compton entry:** The Nobel facts page is too thin for experiment, momentum-transfer formula, and chronology. Add the
  1923 scattering paper; include publication metadata consistently.
- **Davisson–Germer:** This primary citation is strong and DOI-stable. It omits G. P. Thomson despite the prose naming his
  independent experiment; add the corresponding primary paper and sources for the single-electron/interference scope.
- **2022 Nobel summary:** Useful overview of the prize, but it cannot replace Clauser/Freedman, Aspect, and modern Bell-
  test papers for experimental claims. Zeilinger appears in the reference title but is mostly absent from the narrative,
  exposing mismatch between source and prose coverage.
- **Hensen 2015:** Strong primary anchor for one loophole-closing test. The prose says “several groups,” so also cite the
  contemporary photon and atom/other major experiments and a statistics review; one paper cannot prove plural coverage.
- **Transistor history:** Museum chronology is appropriate for public history, but “demonstrated at Bell Labs in 1947”
  should ideally cite Bell Labs archives/primary patent or technical publication. Add access date because exhibits move.
- **BCS:** Excellent primary source for conventional microscopic superconductivity. The prose must retain “conventional”
  because this paper does not explain all superconductors.
- **SEP EPR/Bell:** High-quality living secondary references and appropriate for interpretation/theorem nuance. Record
  edition/revision dates and authors; naked entry titles make a mutable encyclopedia page hard to reproduce.
- **Bell 1964:** Essential primary source. Bibliography should include volume/pages/DOI and clarify that experimental CHSH
  discussions need Clauser–Horne–Shimony–Holt 1969, not Bell alone.
- **Ekert 1991:** Strong primary support for Bell-based QKD, but not BB84 or generic QKD implementation/security claims.
  Add protocol-security references separately.
- **Teleportation 1993:** Strong primary source, though “et al.” hides all authors in a list otherwise often exhaustive;
  choose one citation style consistently and include DOI/volume/pages.
- **Raussendorf–Briegel 2001:** Appropriate original one-way/cluster-state anchor. Adaptive measurement/feedforward and
  resource-state claims should map to exact passages or an explanatory follow-up.
- **Formatting:** Raw autolinks are usable but author initials, complete titles, journals, volumes, pages, years, DOIs,
  and consistent capitalization are uneven. Adopt one formal style and archive stable DOI links where possible.
- **Reader entertainment: 2.5/5.** An annotated bibliography can be inviting, but these entries mostly alternate terse
  labels and URLs. One sentence explaining why each source is useful/limited would reward further reading.
- **Unit completion:** Lines 1323–1370 inspected in full, including the bibliography contract and every entry from Planck
  through measurement-based computation.

##### References — formalism through early algorithms (lines 1371–1415)

- **Schlosshauer:** A strong peer-reviewed review for decoherence/measurement/interpretation boundaries. It cannot alone
  support specific open-system engineering claims; include DOI and clarify which subsection anchors the mixture sidebar.
- **Dirac 1939:** Directly supports the new-notation date and is exactly the primary source the prose needs. Add volume,
  issue, pages, DOI and verify whether earlier bra/ket components or the word “bra-ket” affect the categorical
  “introduced” claim.

##### Core thesis (lines 51–71)

- **Central sentence:** It offers a coherent physics→formalism→information→engineering arc, but “not weird mathematics”
  accepts the pejorative frame and then overcorrects. The mathematics was developed partly within pure mathematics and
  theoretical physics, not only as forced reaction; say the formalism is empirically motivated rather than arbitrary.
- **Century-long sequence:** Approximate scope is fine from 1900 onward, but computation/information roots and present-day
  engineering extend beyond a neat century. “Failed models forced” and “quantum computation emerged” impose inevitability
  and a single causal chain where multiple communities, contingencies, and reciprocal theory/experiment existed.
- **Information wording:** Information theory did not “make computation physical.” Shannon mathematized communication;
  Landauer tied logically irreversible information processing to thermodynamics; Bennett showed reversible computation.
  Rewrite this clause because the current version collapses the chapter’s own careful distinctions.
- **Developer pattern:** The numbered lifecycle is highly legible and useful as a narrative organizer. It resembles a
  software-rewrite myth: edge cases may be central regimes, patches can remain valid approximations, old abstractions
  survive in bounded domains, and formalization/technology co-evolve rather than form waterfall stages.
- **Step 4/5:** Classical abstraction did not globally fail and then get replaced; it remains the effective model at
  suitable scales. Change to “reveals a domain boundary” and “a more general model is constructed,” which teaches better
  engineering practice too.
- **Step 6/7:** Models are formal from their introduction to varying degrees, and old quantum theory already generated
  technologies/measurements. Avoid suggesting formalism mechanically turns into technology; include experimental control,
  fabrication, institutions, and feedback from engineering.
- **Causal scaffolding:** This phrase is the document’s strongest editorial north star. It should be operationalized: each
  historical subsection must end with the exact later concept it motivates, while anecdotes without such payoff are cut
  or boxed.
- **Reader entertainment: 4/5.** The eight-step escalation is satisfying and developer-friendly. Its very neatness is
  also the intellectual danger: experienced readers may recognize a post-hoc rewrite narrative masquerading as history.
- **Unit completion:** Lines 51–71 inspected in full, including the thesis blockquote, every lifecycle step, developer-
  audience rationale, causal-scaffolding claim, and divider.
